svg.text: Rimclip — a captive disc on the rim, and a tap
Design drawing, millimetres. Not a tested prototype. Stainless only. No plastic on a gas rim.
milk surface, ~67 below the rim for 500 mL in a 14 cm pot
1 · Jaw grips the rim (slot 2.6). The arm stays out of the flame.
2 · Notched disc (Ø40) lies in the surface the whole time and cuts the skin.
3 · Loose head taps the anvil when bubbles shake the disc. That is the noise.
A latch that falls only when foam reaches it is the wrong trigger. Foam crosses the rim in about 2 s in the model.
Milk itself swells only about 1.4 mm from fridge to boil, so “expansion” is not enough motion either.

g.text: SS304 wire, 2.5–3 mm, one piece for jaw and arm
SS304 disc, 40 mm × 1.2 mm, six notches, captive pin
Loose striker on the same pin, head Ø5
Set for a 14 cm pot, 500 mL
Drop of the arm, wire centre: 67
Disc centre in from the rim slot: 52
Disc Ø40 × 1.2, six notches, pin Ø2.2
The tap may be too quiet next door.
Breaking the skin may only delay the spill,
the way a spoon does, unless Σ falls enough
that Π drops under 1. That factor is unmeasured.
